subject: Clarify licensed stack + support tiers for VPC pilot
messages:
From: Jason Liu <jason.liu@harborhealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Clarify licensed stack + support tiers for VPC pilot

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Harbor Health is interested in a VPC/private deployment for a clinical routing pilot. Before we take this to procurement, I need a clear breakdown of how you license the stack (base license vs. per-GPU/runtime entitlements), what you charge as the platform service charge (we saw this in the deck but need specifics), and the support tiers and their SLAs.

Two quick details from our side: expected steady-state for pilot is 2 reserved GPUs, burst to 4 for monthly training windows; data residency in us-central and retention of logs for 3 years. Any migration/transition credits for initial on-prem setup would help our budget ask.

Can you send a short proposal and a pricing worksheet we can share with procurement?

Thanks,
Jason
Jason Liu
Director, Platform Engineering
Harbor Health

Attachment: Harbor_Questionnaire.docx (application/msword)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jason Liu <jason.liu@harborhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify licensed stack + support tiers for VPC pilot

Hi Jason — appreciate the details and the clear asks. Attached is a preliminary pricing grid (Pricing_Grid_v3.xlsx) and a short SOW template (HarborHealth_SOW_v1.pdf) to populate with exact node counts and cutover milestones. Summary below to speed procurement review: 

- Licensing: Annual licensed stack fee (covers control plane software + commercial runtime) + per-GPU runtime entitlements (billed monthly). License tiers are based on max reserved GPUs: Small (1–4 GPUs), Medium (5–16 GPUs), Large (17+).
- Platform service charge: applied as a percent on top of base license to cover managed control plane + monitoring; typically 18% for private deployments.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 24h ticket triage), Premium (24/7 with 1-hr critical response), Enterprise (dedicated TAM + quarterly reviews + faster SLAs). SLA credits are tiered; details in worksheet.
- Migration credit: we can offer a one-time migration credit that reduces the first-year license by a fixed amount, subject to a committed term.

Before I draft a formal offer: what term length is Harbor comfortable committing to (12 vs 24 months)? If you can confirm term and an expected date for cutover, I’ll pull in Ben (Commercial) and Neha (Legal/Support) for pricing & compliance items.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Pricing_Grid_v3.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jason Liu <jason.liu@harborhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify licensed stack + support tiers for VPC pilot

Jason — looping in a quick commercial note so procurement has options. Two practical offers that map to what you asked:

Option A (12-month, low friction):
- Small-tier license (covers up to 4 reserved GPUs) + per-GPU runtime entitlements at listed rate.
- Platform service charge: 18% of base license.
- Standard support.
- No migration credit unless you upgrade to Premium tier.

Option B (24-month, better unit economics):
- 10% off base license for a 24-month committed term.
- One-time migration credit equivalent to 1 month's base license applied to Year 1 invoice.
- Platform service charge reduced to 12% (we absorb part of control-plane ops cost for commitment).
- Upgrade to Premium support at a 20% discounted uplift for Year 1.

If Harbor can sign a 24-month term we can be flexible on the migration credit and platform charge. Priyom — can you confirm whether we can push to 15% discount instead of 10% if they add the TAM (Enterprise support) at contract signature?

Thanks,
Ben

On internal notes: mark this as a strategic healthcare logo; we should consider a slightly more generous migration credit if the regional team wants a reference customer.
From: Jason Liu <jason.liu@harborhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: enterprise-ops@harborhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-18T13:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify licensed stack + support tiers for VPC pilot

Thanks Ben and Lauren — that framing is helpful. Harbor prefers a two-year commitment if the economics are right. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal side:

1) Data residency clause and audit log retention (3-year retention) — can we get explicit language?
2) Request for a migration credit that covers part of our on-prem engineering lift (we estimate ~120 engineering hours).
3) Can you confirm whether platform service charge is invoiced monthly or as part of an annual invoice?

I've attached our questionnaire with a few compliance callouts. If you can respond to the questionnaire and give a short redline-ready term sheet, procurement can move quickly.

Regards,
Jason

Attachment: Harbor_Questionnaire.docx (application/msword)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jason Liu <jason.liu@harborhealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T15:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify licensed stack + support tiers for VPC pilot

Hi Jason — thanks for the questionnaire; we reviewed the compliance items and can confirm the following in a redline-ready clause set: 

- Data residency: we will deploy the control plane in your us-central VPC and retain audit logs for 3 years. We will include an appendix specifying the logging schema and access controls.
- Migration credit: we can cover up to 80 hours of professional services effort as a credit against Year 1 invoice, or convert to an equivalent USD credit (~$30k) if you prefer. The credit is contingent on a 24-month committed term.
- Platform service charge billing: invoiced monthly, itemized on your invoice; for a 24-month term we can reduce the rate to 12% for Year 1 then tier to 15% Year 2.
- SLA credits: Premium and Enterprise tiers include faster incident response; SLA credits are capped per quarter and defined in the SLA schedule.

If Harbor signs a 24-month term with Enterprise support we can increase the migration credit to cover the 120 engineering hours you estimated (subject to SOW verification). I will draft the clause language and share a redline in the next 24 hours.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jason Liu <jason.liu@harborhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T16:10:00-08:00
Subject: Final — Proposed offer: licensed stack + transition credit

Jason — based on the internal alignment here’s a concise offer you can take to procurement today: 

Proposed commercial summary (Harbor Health)
- Term: 24 months (preferred)
- Licensed stack: Small-tier license covering up to 4 reserved GPUs; Year 1 base license $150,000, Year 2 base license $155,000 (list).
- Runtime entitlements: per-GPU runtime billed monthly at listed rate (worksheet).
- Platform service charge: 12% in Year 1, 15% in Year 2 (invoiced monthly, itemized).
- Support: Enterprise support in Year 1 (dedicated TAM + quarterly reviews) at a 20% discounted uplift off published Enterprise price.
- Migration / transition credit: $60,000 credit applied to Year 1 invoice (covers up to 120 engineering hours). Credit contingent on 24-month signed term and execution of SOW within 60 days of signature.
- Compliance: Data residency in us-central, audit log retention 3 years — we will include explicit language in the SOW appendix.

Next steps: I’ll draft a 1-page term sheet and send for your review; once agreed we’ll route to DocuSign and legal for signature. If you want, we can also line up a kickoff call with our deployment engineers next week (we can demo the migration checklist).

If procurement is comfortable with these bullets I’ll convert to a redline-ready term sheet and push the HubSpot deal to Contract stage.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to pilot.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: HarborHealth_SOW_v1.pdf, Pricing_Grid_v3.xlsx
